name: How do you protect finished surfaces during luxury installation?

mainEntity.name: How are expensive floors, cabinets, and fixtures protected while other trades are still working?
mainEntity.text: How are expensive floors, cabinets, and fixtures protected while other trades are still working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Protecting finished surfaces is critical on luxury projects because one careless trade can damage expensive work that was already completed. The installer should plan the sequence so vulnerable items like flooring, cabinets, stone, and fixtures are installed only when the surrounding work is ready. Temporary coverings, dust barriers, corner protection, and clear walk paths help reduce scratches and chips. High-end finishes are especially vulnerable to construction dust, adhesive residue, dropped tools, and paint overspray. Homeowners should ask how the team will protect surfaces during demolition, fabrication deliveries, plumbing rough-in, painting, and final cleanup. It is also important that each trade knows which areas are complete and which are still open for work. A well-managed luxury job protects the finish quality from the start instead of trying to repair damage at the end.
acceptedAnswer.description: Finished surfaces should be protected with the right coverings, edge guards, dust barriers, and sequencing so later trades do not damage earlier work. Luxury projects often require strict jobsite protection because stone, wood, glass, and plated finishes can scratch or stain easily during construction.
